greTransport.label: Transport mode

dns.success: Node DNS is set to the Iran server IP.
dns.needsHealthy: Activate the tunnel and wait for a fresh healthy report before setting DNS.

title: Tunnel Management
description: GRE and WireGuard are network interfaces. GOST, Backhaul, and Rathole are port-forwarding services and do not have a separate interface.
demoActions: Start, stop, restart, and delete do not create a real interface.
interfaceState: Interface {name} is {state} in the data model.
forwarderKind: This technology is a port-forwarding service and has no network interface.
deleteBody: The tunnel is removed from the sample list and dependent nodes appear offline.
monitorDescription: Registered topology and probes reported by the Agent.
demoDescription: The topology and actions on this page are simulated.
operationalDescription: Preview the registered bundles for both hosts and follow the installation steps.

wizard.title: Tunnel wizard
wizard.description: Create a tunnel in nine steps. Deployment only changes demo data.
wizard.note: No GRE or WireGuard packet, and no GOST service, runs on the host.
wizard.registered: Tunnel registered in the sample list

check.same: The two servers must not be the same
check.mtuReady: MTU is within the allowed range

recipe.title: Build a two-host bundle
recipe.failed: Could not download the bundle specification.
recipe.forwarder: Download the specification for both hosts. In the local input file, specify the binary, hash, and reviewed configuration for each side.
recipe.interface: Download the path specification and build the hashed bundles on the operator computer. When a port is registered, the source bundle includes GOST. For an arm64 source, add ‎--gost-architecture arm64‎. For WireGuard, key files and separate UDP ports are provided.

deployment.coordinated: Coordinated deployment of both tunnel ends
deployment.disabled: Operational provisioning is disabled in the backend settings.
deployment.noBundle: No bundle matches the current path settings.
deployment.tcpFrom: The current plan forwards TCP from port
deployment.afterInstall: After both sides are installed, a fresh path probe confirms the result.
deployment.confirmBody: This request reserves both hosts and queues the bundles shown.
deployment.standbyReady: · the foreign side is already prepared.
deployment.deployBody: Both Agents receive the installation job. The result is recorded after the path check.
deployment.teardownBody: Installed configuration is removed from the hosts, and the tunnel record remains for a later deployment.
deployment.rebuildTitle: Rebuild the tunnel on both servers
deployment.rebuildBody: The previous installation is removed and the approved plan is installed again on both sides.
deployment.deletePanelTitle: Remove the path from the panel inventory
deployment.deletePanelBody: The tunnel is disconnected from its node automatically. If both the Iran and foreign agents are reachable, the tunnel is also removed from those servers. If they are not reachable, the tunnel and all of its settings are deleted from the panel, and the next install of the same path starts from scratch.
deployment.rollbackIranBody: The Iran bundle returns to the previously registered version.
deployment.rollbackBothBody: The Iran bundle returns first, then the foreign bundle, to the previously registered version.
deployment.reviewIranBody: After the ambiguous state on the Iran server is resolved, record the result.
deployment.reviewBothBody: After the ambiguous state on both hosts is reviewed and resolved, record the result.

warning.tls_certificate: The foreign host's V2bX logs contain a certificate issuance or validation error, and the destination service port is unreachable. Fix SSL and V2bX on the foreign host, then retry tunnel installation. The panel does not change certificates automatically.
warning.destination_service: The destination service port is unreachable. Check V2bX, the node port, and SSL on the foreign host. This alone does not mean the tunnel protocol is blocked. Fix the service, then retry installation.

failure.listener_conflict: A different managed service owns this port. Choose independent tunnel ports.
failure.reverted: Installation or verification failed. Changes were rolled back.
failure.tcp_target_unreachable: The destination service did not accept TCP on the configured target port. Changes were rolled back.
failure.tcp_forward_unreachable: The destination accepted TCP, but the forwarded port did not. Changes were rolled back.

check.tcp: Check port forwarding and the TCP connection to the destination
check.control: Verify the running service and connected client control channel

activation.failed: Failed; check DNS settings and retry

failover.title: Failover management
failover.description: State machine, policy, and outage simulation. A DNS change does not guarantee immediate client migration.
failover.note: Because of TTL, resolver cache, and open connections, a domain switch can keep users on the previous path for several minutes. Concurrent actions and actions inside the cooldown period are blocked.
failover.siblingImpact: A primary server failure also affects {count} other nodes that are still active on the same host: {names}.
failover.operationalDescription: Independent path evidence, DNS preflight, and the decision history for a move.
failover.operationalNote: An approved plan can run against the registered record when DNS changes are enabled. The result is checked after TTL elapses.
failover.firstTitle: Register the first node for failover
failover.firstBody: Register the V2Board node and its tunnel paths for monitoring. The DNS change policy is then available on this page.
failover.triggerServerPing: Iran server ping to the panel is down
failover.triggerLoss: Packet loss on the Iran server ping to the panel
failover.triggerTunnelPing: Internal tunnel IP ping is down
failover.telegram: Telegram alert after the DNS change
failover.confirmationsLine: Independent confirmation of the destination {current} of {required} · sources with consecutive failures {failures}
failover.automaticNotReady: Automatic policy conditions are not met
failover.registerBody: The path plan from {from} to {to} is registered for review.
failover.noPlans: No plan has been registered for this node yet.
failover.stale: The evidence or configuration has changed.
failover.approveBody: Review the planned move from {from} to {to}.
failover.rejectAutomatic: Rejecting the plan delays the next automatic attempt by at least two minutes.
failover.rejectManual: Rejecting the plan allows a new plan to be registered for this node.
failover.executeBody: The approved plan is queued to change the authoritative record.
failover.advanceBody: The recorded stage moves forward for apply, verification, or rollback.
failover.reconcileBody: The current record is compared with the registered versions, and the execution status is updated when they match.
failover.requestRollbackBody: If the record still belongs to this execution, the previous value is restored.
